narratives.text: Jupiter is one of five bipolar engine governors and the A0 anchor of the 7-35 family, rooted on state 1453 — Aeolian — with the pitch field {0,2,3,5,7,8,10}. The field is achiral: it coincides with its own inversion, and that symmetry is what lets a bipolar engine govern both directions of a degree without re-registration. The profile is bound to a photonic record at 470 nm (#4488FF), the deepest blue in the spectrum of the seven offices, and references six landform pools, the most stable basin ledger among the governors. Its intrinsic fingerprint is pinned at build time and resolves with zero scope bindings, so every reference issued from this profile lands inside the compiled universe. As a bipolar engine governor, Jupiter does not merely stand for the Aeolian mode: it is the turning mechanism itself — the same field seen from either side of the tonic seam, ready to phase in either direction.

Mars is the bipolar engine governor rooted on state 1717 — Mixolydian — carrying the 7-35 field {0,2,4,5,7,9,10}. It is the only canonical profile whose root mode places the natural seventh at the top of the field, and it holds the longest landform ledger of the seven offices: seven pools. Its photonic record sits at 580 nm (#FFD700), the amber band shared with the red planet of the same name. The field is achiral and anchored at tier A0 with zero unresolved scope bindings; the intrinsic fingerprint bound at build time makes the pin tamper-evident. Mixolydian with a natural seventh is the traditional workhorse of secular scale, and Mars carries that role into the compiled universe: the field most often found at the boundary between modal identity and functional harmony, and the engine best placed to turn that boundary into a phase shift.

Mercury is the bipolar engine governor rooted on state 1709 — Dorian — with the 7-35 field {0,2,3,5,7,9,10}. Dorian is the median mode: its characteristic b3 and natural 6 sit exactly between minor and major, and Mercury's ledger reflects that mediation with the leanest landform count among the governors at five pools. Its photonic record is green, 530 nm (#44BB44), the midpoint of the visible band — fitting for the office that stands between the poles. Achiral at anchor tier A0 with zero unresolved scope bindings, the profile is pinned by an intrinsic fingerprint recomputed at every build. As an engine governor, Mercury is the mode of passage: the field whose two whole-tone halves are separated by exactly one semitone, and which therefore shifts cleanly in either direction of the tonic seam.

The Moon is one of the two monopolar luminaries in the canonical registry, and the only profile whose root state carries the natural major field. Rooted on state 2741 — Ionian — with pitch set {0,2,4,5,7,9,11}, it is achiral at anchor tier A0 and resolves zero scope bindings. Its photonic record is the warmest of the office band: 610 nm (#FF8C00), a harvest-orange at the transition between amber and red. It references six landform pools. As a monopolar luminary the Moon has no inverse-facing engine: it radiates from a single pole, the field of the major scale itself, the most familiar of all seven-note shapes. It is pinned by its intrinsic fingerprint and serves as the reference point against which the five bipolar engines phase their seams.

Saturn is a bipolar engine governor rooted on state 1387 — Locrian — the darkest of the seven modal roots, with the 7-35 field {0,1,3,5,6,8,10}. Locrian is the only mode whose tonic triad is diminished; its b5 places the tritone inside the root itself, and Saturn's photonic record answers with the highest-energy signature in the spectrum: 400 nm (#9400D3), deep violet. Achiral at anchor tier A0 with six landform pools and zero unresolved scope bindings, it is bound by its intrinsic fingerprint at build time. As the engine of the unstable root, Saturn is the governor of the edge: the field whose seam is hardest to hold, and therefore the office that most exercises the phase and degree machinery of the registry when it turns.

The Sun is the second of the two monopolar luminaries and the only canonical root in the raised-fourth position. Rooted on state 2773 — Lydian — with pitch set {0,2,4,6,7,9,11}, the field carries the sharpest internal interval in the registry: the augmented fourth between tonic and degree 4, which is exactly what makes the Lydian field luminous. Its photonic record sits at the red end of the band, 700 nm (#FF4444), and its landform ledger is the shortest of the seven offices at four pools — a bright field holding few basins. Achiral at anchor tier A0 with zero unresolved scope bindings and a pinned intrinsic fingerprint, the Sun is the counterpole of the Moon: where Ionian is the familiar major field, Lydian is its raised, unresolved cousin, forever leaning one semitone past rest.

Venus is the bipolar engine governor rooted on state 1451 — Phrygian — with the 7-35 field {0,1,3,5,7,8,10}. Phrygian is the minor mode with the lowered second: the b2 sits directly above the tonic, giving the field its characteristic semitone opening and its tension at the bottom of the scale. Its photonic record is violet at 430 nm (#8B008B), the mirror of Saturn at the opposite edge of the band. Achiral at anchor tier A0 with six landform pools and zero unresolved scope bindings, the profile is bound by its intrinsic fingerprint. As an engine governor, Venus governs the most compressed step in the mode system — the b2 seam — and is the office through which the registry's lowering operators and their inverses find their most natural phase surface.

The modal successor is the only complete operator in the registry: total over all 462 rooted weight-seven states, with no partial-domain restriction, image equal to domain, and every application formally projected. Applying M re-roots the unchanged pitch-class set at its next ascending scale tone; composed seven times it returns to identity, which is why its inverse is written M^6 and why M is its own conjugate. Because a re-rooting preserves the pitch-class set exactly, M carries 182 structural edges and zero field projections — pure topology, no hamming noise. Its audited union coverage is 39.4%: 280 of the 462 formal applications lie outside the MODAL_SUCCESSOR projection gap and remain unprojected, marking where the formal modal operator exceeds the canonical witness. As the self-inverse root of the commutation class, M is excluded from the pairwise commutation matrix by design: it is the axis against which the other fourteen operators measure their phase.

R1 is the root-phase raise: it moves the tonic seam one semitone up, retaining the other six absolute pitches, then renormalizes the new root to 0. Its domain rule requires pitch class 1 to be absent — a colliding root phase fails before projection. Within its partial domain of 210 states the operator is total; the audited union coverage of 85.7% is the highest of any partial operator, with 175 applications carried by field edges against 29 structural witnesses. Its inverse is L1 and its conjugate is R7, both under the Saturn degree governor. The 30 unprojected applications are exactly where the PHASE_SHIFT field evidence runs out and the complete phase operator still acts.

L1 is the root-phase lower, the mirror of R1: the tonic seam moves one semitone down, the other six absolute pitches are retained, and the new root is renormalized to 0. It is defined when pitch class 11 is absent, applies to all 210 states of its partial domain, and achieves the joint highest audited coverage of the registry at 85.7% — 175 field edges plus 29 structural witnesses. Its inverse is R1 and its conjugate is L7, governed by Saturn. Thirty of its 210 formal applications fall in the unprojected gap. Where R1 raises the seam into the light, L1 drops it into the shadow; together they are the registry's canonical demonstration that phase is a direction, not a state.

R2 is the fixed-degree raise for Degree 2, governed by Jupiter: the pitch at ordered degree 2 is replaced by +1 semitone, defined only when the move causes no collision and does not cross the rooted boundary. It applies to 210 states, image equal to domain, with 29 structural witnesses and 25 field edges — an audited union coverage of 21.0%, with 166 of its formal applications left unprojected. Its inverse is L2 and its conjugate is R1, the first link of the raise chain. As the shift nearest the tonic, R2 documents the first articulation a mode makes away from its seam.

L2 is the fixed-degree lower for Degree 2, governed by Jupiter: the pitch at ordered degree 2 moves down one semitone whenever the move is collision-free and respects the rooted boundary. Its partial domain covers 210 states; audited union coverage is 21.0% (29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges) and 166 of 210 formal applications fall in the unprojected gap. Its inverse is R2 and its conjugate is L1. Immediately beside the tonic, degree 2 is the seam's first neighbor, and L2 is the operator that articulates the mode's opening half-step from below.

R3 is the fixed-degree raise for Degree 3, governed by Mars: the pitch at ordered degree 3 is raised one semitone where the move is collision-free and stays within the rooted boundary. It applies to 210 states with image equal to domain; audited union coverage is 21.0%, supported by 29 structural witnesses and 25 field edges, with 166 of 210 formal applications unprojected. Its inverse is L3 and its conjugate is R2. Degree 3 is where the mode's quality — major or minor — is decided, and R3 is the operator that pushes the field across that quality boundary.

L3 is the fixed-degree lower for Degree 3, governed by Mars: the pitch at ordered degree 3 drops one semitone where the move is collision-free and respects the rooted boundary. It is total over its 210-state partial domain, with an audited union coverage of 21.0% (29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges) and 166 of 210 formal applications left unprojected. Its inverse is R3 and its conjugate is L2. Degree 3 is the quality degree of the mode, and L3 is the operator that pulls the field down to its minor variant — the first step of the lowering chain.

R4 is the fixed-degree raise for Degree 4, governed by the Sun: the pitch at ordered degree 4 is raised one semitone where the move is collision-free and stays within the rooted boundary. It applies to 210 states; audited union coverage is 21.0%, with 29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges, and 166 of 210 formal applications unprojected. Its inverse is L4 and its conjugate is R3. Degree 4 is the pivotal note of the Lydian field — the raised fourth is what makes that mode luminous — and R4 is the registry's record of the pivot itself.

L4 is the fixed-degree lower for Degree 4, governed by the Sun: the pitch at ordered degree 4 drops one semitone where the move is collision-free and respects the rooted boundary. Its partial domain covers 210 states with an audited union coverage of 21.0% (29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges); 166 of 210 formal applications remain unprojected. Its inverse is R4 and its conjugate is L3. Degree 4 is the tritone-adjacent pivot of the modal system, and L4 is the operator that releases the field's raised fourth back to rest.

R5 is the fixed-degree raise for Degree 5, governed by Venus: the pitch at ordered degree 5 is raised one semitone where the move is collision-free and stays within the rooted boundary. It applies to 210 states with image equal to domain; audited union coverage is 21.0% (29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges), with 166 of 210 formal applications unprojected. Its inverse is L5 and its conjugate is R4. Degree 5 is the dominant degree — the natural anchor of the fields above the tonic — and R5 sharpens the mode's most active harmonic tone.

L5 is the fixed-degree lower for Degree 5, governed by Venus: the pitch at ordered degree 5 drops one semitone where the move is collision-free and respects the rooted boundary. It is total over its 210-state partial domain, with an audited union coverage of 21.0% (29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges) and 166 of 210 formal applications unprojected. Its inverse is R5 and its conjugate is L4. Degree 5 is the dominant degree, and L5 is the operator that flattens it — the registry's canonical record of the lowered fifth at the edge of the modal field.

R6 is the fixed-degree raise for Degree 6, governed by Mercury: the pitch at ordered degree 6 is raised one semitone where the move is collision-free and stays within the rooted boundary. It applies to 210 states; audited union coverage is 21.0%, with 29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges, and 166 of 210 formal applications unprojected. Its inverse is L6 and its conjugate is R5. Degree 6 is the upper neighbor of the fifth — the note that separates the two whole-tone halves of the mode — and R6 records the registry's upward articulation of that boundary.

L6 is the fixed-degree lower for Degree 6, governed by Mercury: the pitch at ordered degree 6 drops one semitone where the move is collision-free and respects the rooted boundary. Its partial domain covers 210 states with an audited union coverage of 21.0% (29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges); 166 of 210 formal applications remain unprojected. Its inverse is R6 and its conjugate is L5. Degree 6 is the upper neighbor of the fifth, and L6 is the operator that lowers it — flattening the sixth is what turns a major field toward the Dorian median.

R7 is the fixed-degree raise for Degree 7, governed by the Moon: the pitch at ordered degree 7 is raised one semitone where the move is collision-free and stays within the rooted boundary. It applies to 210 states with image equal to domain; audited union coverage is 21.0% (29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges), with 166 of 210 formal applications unprojected. Its inverse is L7 and its conjugate is R6, the final link of the raise chain. Degree 7 is the leading tone — the note that pulls back to the tonic — and R7 is the operator that raises the field to its sharpest seventh.

L7 is the fixed-degree lower for Degree 7, governed by the Moon: the pitch at ordered degree 7 drops one semitone where the move is collision-free and respects the rooted boundary. It is total over its 210-state partial domain, with an audited union coverage of 21.0% (29 structural witnesses, 25 field edges) and 166 of 210 formal applications unprojected. Its inverse is R7 and its conjugate is L6, closing the lowering chain. Degree 7 is the leading tone, and L7 is the operator that flattens it to a natural seventh — the registry's canonical record of the Mixolydian turn at the top of the field.
